newsitem.title: singapore: Two Singaporeans charged over injured Bangladeshi.
newsitem.headline: Two Singaporeans charged over injured Bangladeshi.

text.p: Two Singaporeans were charged on Monday with endangering human life after an injured illegal Bangladeshi worker was dumped in a drainage ditch, Singapore state television reported.
The two men were charged after Mohammed Bashar, hit on the head by a lift on a construction site, was dumped instead of being taken to hospital.
He is permanently paralysed from the waist down and the judge called for stronger charges, the television report said.
It said the judge called the current charges "ridiculous" because they carried a maximum sentence of three months in jail or a Singapore $250 (US$175) fine.
The television report named the two men charged as Bashar's employers Koh Tiong Watt, 38, and Lau Chai Hock, 44.
It said they were freed on bail of S$30,000.
Money and good have poured in for Bashar, 24.
"I was with him on Sunday and by then he had received about S$1,300 and many visitors," a Bangladesh diplomat told Reuters. The television report said that by Monday that sum had risen to S$2,000.
Bashar has told reporters he lay writhing in agony in the drainage ditch for two hours in December before his cries for help attracted the attention of a passing army jeep.
His plight came to light on Friday after police confirmed they had arrested one man and were hunting for a second in connection with the incident.
Staff at the hospital where Bashar is being treated told Singapore's Sunday Times newspaper they had received more than 50 calls to ask about his condition and make donations.

The newspaper quoted several visitors as saying they were appalled such a thing could happen in Singapore, which has been cracking down recently on companies, many of them in the construction industry, which employ illegal workers.
Singapore's Ministry of Labour said on Monday it had fined one construction company S$145,200 after a raid turned up 33 illegal workers in the latest action in the crackdown.
Bashar's medical bills have been met so far by Singapore authorities, said the Bangladesh official, who asked not to be identified.
"We are in touch with the Singapore authorities about how they will deal with this inhuman behaviour. We want stern action taken to ensure such things never happen again," he said.
Bangladesh was talking to Singapore about compensation payments for the injuries, he added.
Singapore deports illegal workers, but police said on Friday no decision had been made on whether to send Bashar home.
Bashar said he found after arriving in Singapore that the work permit he paid S$6,000 for back home was a forgery.
